title: Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Multiple Comparisons
description: Testing differences in means across three or more independent groups with post-hoc family-wise error rate control.
conditions: One continuous outcome metric and one discrete grouping variable with 3 or more levels
Normally distributed residuals and homogeneity of variance across groups
recommended_methods: One-Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) for single grouping factor
Welch's ANOVA when group variances are unequal (Levene's test p < 0.05)
Tukey's Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) post-hoc test for pairwise comparisons
selection_rules: Only run post-hoc pairwise tests if overall omnibus ANOVA F-test is statistically significant (p < 0.05)
Use Tukey HSD for all-pairwise comparisons to maintain Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER) at 0.05
If comparing multiple treatment groups against a single control group, use Dunnett's test instead of Tukey HSD
limitations: Standard ANOVA is sensitive to severe variance heterogeneity when group sample sizes are unequal
Omnibus significance only indicates at least one group differs; it does not indicate which one
source: Tukey (1949) Comparing Individual Means in the Analysis of Variance
